subject: Pricing exhibit: commit swell / proration language & cap/floor true-up — clarification requested
messages:
From: Susan James <susan.james@optimahealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing exhibit redline — proration and "commit swell" mechanics

Hi Sergio / Lauren,

Thanks for sending the draft pricing exhibit. We reviewed it with procurement and finance and have a few sticking points we need clarified before we take the redline to our legal team. Attached is our annotated PDF with the proposed edits. High level:

- The "commit swell" protection in Section 3 reads like an annualized true-up but doesn't specify proration for the initial/termination partial months. We need an explicit example (monthly invoice + true-up) that demonstrates the math.
- The cap/floor language references a "stabilization band" but doesn't define how credits apply if usage spikes above the cap mid-billing period. Will credits be applied pro rata or only at true-up?
- We're asking for an explicit carveout for restricted workloads (PHI) so they don't count toward burst credits while we validate on-prem routing.

Possible outcomes we'd accept: clear proration language for partial months + worked examples, or a short 12-month smoothing approach in lieu of per-month true-ups.

Can you send us a clean redline that: 1) clarifies proration, 2) states whether cap/floor credits apply monthly or at true-up, and 3) adds the restricted workload carveout? If you need, we'll hop on a 30-minute call.

Attachments: Optima_Redline_Pricing_Exhibit.pdf, redline-pricing-comments-Optima.txt

Best,
Susan James
Senior Procurement Manager
Optima Health
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Susan James <susan.james@optimahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit redline — proration and "commit swell" mechanics

Susan — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated PDF. Quick response with a proposal to keep momentum:

Summary of what we'll deliver as a clean redline by EOD tomorrow:
- Explicit proration clause for partial months: "Monthly invoices will be prorated based on calendar days in the billing month; true-up calculations will reflect prorated usage for initial and termination partial months. Example calculation added as Appendix A."
- Cap/floor credit timing: two options in the redline (please indicate preference):
  Option A — Monthly application: credits/charges applied each monthly invoice pro rata for days where usage exceeds the cap or falls below the floor.
  Option B — Quarterly true-up: credits/charges calculated at quarter-end true-up and applied to the subsequent invoice (limits volatility).
- Restricted workload carveout: add explicit exclusion that workloads classified as "regulated: PHI/PCI" by Optima will be excluded from burst-credit calculations until VPC/on-prem routing is validated in production or an agreed acceptance test is passed.

Ask: please tell us whether you prefer Option A (monthly) or Option B (quarterly). If neither, we can propose a hybrid (monthly smoothing with quarterly settlement).

I've looped in Lauren for finance signs and Marissa/Karthik from legal/ops to draft the suggested wording and the example workbook.

I'll attach an initial working workbook to illustrate the math in both options. If that looks right we will convert into formal redline language and send to your counsel.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit redline — proration and "commit swell" mechanics

Sergio / Lauren — attaching a short workbook and draft redline language. Key comments from legal/finance:

- Draft language for Appendix A (worked example) included in the attached pricing-workbook-optima.xlsx. It shows both Option A (monthly pro rata application) and Option B (quarterly true-up) with sample numbers.
- We recommend Option B for larger enterprise deals to reduce month-to-month volatility. Suggest adding a 10% smoothing floor so very small month-over-month variances don't result in micro-invoices. Wording: "Charges or credits calculated at quarterly true-up will not be applied if the net quarterly adjustment is less than 10% of the committed monthly baseline for that quarter; such de minimis adjustments will be carried forward to the next quarter's settlement."
- On the restricted workload carveout: include a short acceptance test (see section 3.2) for on-prem/VPC routing validation. If Optima marks workloads as regulated and acceptance test fails, Redwood will not count that usage toward burst credits until remediation.

I'm attaching pricing-workbook-optima.xlsx and a text redline snippet. If Optima prefers monthly application, we can remove the 10% de minimis threshold.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit redline — proration and "commit swell" mechanics

Sergio / Marissa / Lauren — thanks, the workbook is very helpful. We discussed internally and prefer Option B (quarterly true-up) with the 10% de minimis threshold — it aligns with our payroll cycles and reduces short-term billing churn. We also accept the restricted workload carveout and will provide the initial list of PHI-tagged services by Friday.

Next steps from our side:
- We will provide the PHI workload list and any additional redline comments by Friday, 11/12.
- Please send the formal contract redline (clean tracked changes) and a DocuSign-ready order form reflecting the quarterly true-up and de minimis threshold.
- Let's have a 30-minute call Monday 11/15 at 10:00am PT to finalize.

If you can get the redline to us by EOD 11/10 that gives our legal and procurement time to run it.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this.
